question: An architect finishes a plan mode session where Claude proposed a design for restructuring a shared utilities package used by 12 services. The architect wants Claude to now make the changes exactly as proposed, without re-explaining the reasoning behind each file edit. What should the architect do next?
options: A) Start an entirely new session from scratch and re-describe the utilities package restructuring in full before implementation begins
B) Stay in plan mode indefinitely and have Claude describe each proposed file edit in the chat instead of ever actually making the edit
C) Exit the session without approving anything and instead manually perform the twelve-service restructuring by hand rather than having Claude do it
D) Approve the plan and choose an option that switches the session into an editing mode, so Claude proceeds directly with the approved design
correct_answers: D) Approve the plan and choose an option that switches the session into an editing mode, so Claude proceeds directly with the approved design
explanations: Starting over in a fresh session discards the plan and context Claude already built during the investigation, requiring the architect to redo work that plan mode already completed.
Staying in plan mode keeps edits blocked indefinitely, so the restructuring across the 12 services would never actually be applied to the files.
Manually performing a 12-service restructuring by hand discards the value of having Claude execute the already-approved plan and reintroduces the risk of inconsistent manual changes.

Correct. Approving the plan and choosing an edit-enabling option exits plan mode and switches the session into a mode where Claude proceeds with implementing the design that was just investigated and approved.
